---
title: Employee schema qualification
description: Qualify the employee creation and restoration schema in an exact-source disposable database.
---

Dispatch `employee-schema-contract.yaml` on a published ref whose head is the
reviewed creation/restoration stack commit, and set `source_sha` to that same
full SHA. The workflow rejects a source that differs from the dispatched
(control) commit, so no dispatch input selects code to run in that ref's cache
scope, in particular `main`'s. It keeps the control checkout at the workspace root
for the shared setup action and checks out the same commit under `source/`. Commands run from that
source directory invoke the reviewed control scripts via `../apps` and
`../scripts`; they never substitute current main or
connects to staging or production. Its installed CLI starts a disposable
full-migration Supabase project using the same isolated runner as the Tutoring
contract gates. Startup/reset and each fixture are bounded; an always-run cleanup
step stops only the owned project, without retaining a database backup.

## Employee public-consumer proof

The employee schema workflow's `include_public_consumer` option defaults off and
excludes standalone chat and diagnostic provenance. It preserves the selected SQL
packets and counts while generating types from that owned database, even on the
foundation profile. Before cleanup, the maintained adapter records private employee
function definitions, table columns/RLS and the complete applied migration ledger
as digests before generation, rechecks them after generation, then compiles the current CREATE aliases and RESTORE public imports
against the same artifact. It checks source/control commits, tracked source digests,
repository/run/attempt, isolated project, artifact hash and catalog identity again
after compilation. No SQL or compiler diagnostic values enter the receipt.

The compiler uses `noEmit` with `noCheck: false`, inherits strict repository flags, derives source entries
from actual public package export targets and replaces only the generated schema
inside a disposable Types source copy with the owning dependency links. Its fixture
requires operation identity through both creation names and exercises missing/wrong
UUID, revision, private RPC and private table controls. UUID string syntax remains
owned by runtime validation; TypeScript checks its string representation.
`employeePublicConsumer.sourceCompilerQualified` in `qualification.json` requires
successful generation, compilation, unchanged bindings, SQL qualification, compiler
scratch cleanup and owned database cleanup. Failure, timeout or a skipped compiler
stays false; `emittedPublicPackageQualified` stays false. This source proof does not
replace exact-commit real builds or emitted public package/release acceptance.
Focused regressions live in `scripts/employee-public-consumer-qualification.test.mjs`
and the maintained workflow test. SQL/catalog and same-run generated-schema acceptance
require a separately admitted hosted run; checked-in-schema compiler smoke is only
fixture validation.

The compiler state remains provisional through all optional HTTP/Web runtime work.
Immediately before the existing owned database stop, a lifecycle adapter rechecks
live catalog identity, current source/control binding and the generated artifact
against the original compiler state. A failed check still allows the existing
stop and cleanup proof to run once. After cleanup returns, the adapter rechecks
only the filesystem artifact and source/control binding; it never queries the
destroyed database. Both final fences, SQL/lifecycle success and positive owned
cleanup are required before sourceCompilerQualified can be true. Primary final-check
and cleanup failures remain available together; no unknown operation is retried.

Late-runtime artifact/catalog drift and source/control changes during cleanup are
covered by the root proof regression file. The lifecycle check does not change
packet selection/counts, optional defaults or the existing cleanup ownership rule.

The foundation gate requires all five packets: signup guards (25), administrator
(20), finalization (34), identity contract (52), and restoration (41). Each packet
must emit one complete, sequential, non-skipped pgTAP plan and close its synthetic
transaction with rollback. Missing packets, a different count, failed SQL,
truncated output, or unsuccessful cleanup fail the gate. The private command
output is not uploaded; the small JSON artifact binds the exact source and fixture
hashes to the 172 assertions and cleanup outcome.

Verify the helper with
`node --test apps/database/scripts/employee-schema-tap.test.mjs`.
A green schema result is not native admission/lease/fence qualification, a GoTrue
or provider transaction, employee activation, or production SQL application.
The feedback layer is a separate, default-off selection. In
`employee-schema-contract.yaml`, set `source_sha` to the reviewed clean 40-character
commit and `include_feedback=true`; leave `structured_provenance`,
`include_journal`, `include_personal_journal`, `include_address_migration`,
`include_http`, `include_web_session` and `include_restore` false. The control
checkout must also contain the feedback input, selector and runner wiring.
This profile runs the original 172 employee assertions, then intake34, staff-inbox41
and staff-eligibility31, for 278 total. Existing profiles retain their counts.
Incompatible optional profile combinations fail before database setup.

`include_feedback` selects tests, not migration application or feature activation.
Every profile still applies the complete tracked migration snapshot to its
disposable database, including feedback migrations when present. An older
profile's green receipt retains its original count and does not qualify feedback.
The legacy profile matrix explicitly sets feedback false in each child; the
feedback controls separately test true, including a parent dispatch environment
with feedback enabled. Neither control changes the profile incompatibility guard.

The maintained runner requires hosted Linux with `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`, an exact
HEAD matching `source_sha` and no tracked source modifications. It stages and
byte-compares the complete tracked database snapshot, including all migration
history, before applying it to its derived isolated project. Never simulate these
hosted guards locally. Packet source hashes, strict sequential TAP, rollback,
bounded command deadlines and cleanup of only the exact owned project remain
mandatory. The always-run workflow cleanup step checks retained ownership before
stopping an interrupted project. A successful feedback packet run generates types
from that same database before cleanup; the receipt and artifact retain the digest.
A failed packet does not establish type generation or SQL qualification.

Eligibility qualification must retain an exact-source hosted BEFORE failure and
owned cleanup before changing fixture setup. The observed original fixture failed
its no-membership assertion: ordinary Auth signup inserts a public profile and
unconditionally bootstraps personal membership. Setting the employee marker earlier
alone does not prevent that trigger and also requires a canonical creation intent.

The eligibility fixture constructs a synthetic membership-free actor by suppressing
only `auto_create_personal_workspace_tr` on `public.users` around its two Auth
identity inserts. It first locks `public.users` under the existing SQL lock timeout
to prevent concurrent trigger-state changes, then requires the named trigger, canonical function and normal
`O` enabled state; unexpected state aborts before suppression. The same block
immediately restores `ENABLE TRIGGER` and verifies that exact state before all
thirty-one behavioral assertions. A final non-TAP integrity fence checks the restored
state before `finish()` and rollback. Setup/integrity exceptions fail the packet;
these fences add no pgTAP assertions. Transaction rollback also restores trigger
DDL if setup or later SQL fails; the hosted lifecycle must still prove owned cleanup.
No other trigger, production function, ACL, RLS or membership is changed/deleted.

This constructs an eligibility precondition, not proof that canonical employee
signup lacks personal membership. Keep that observed signup behavior in the parent
residual audit. Do not weaken staff eligibility, remove assertions or substitute a
minimal registry. The candidate preserves the original105 assertions and adds one registry-correlation
assertion, for106 feedback assertions;
require a fresh exact-source hosted AFTER with foundation172, same-database type
generation and positive cleanup. SQL causal controls remain separately admitted
proof. Static fixture inspection and pure parser tests do not execute SQL or
establish AFTER qualification. Feature activation and production remain separate.

### Optional feedback causal qualification

The retained hosted source with eligibility30 passed277 assertions and emitted
types. The new correlation assertion31 and causal helper are a new source unit;
that prior result does not qualify278 or the causal phase. Correlation coverage
uses two existing synthetic Auth identities: temporarily give registry row A
actor B's distinct valid corporate email, require B to remain denied, restore
A's email and compare the complete registry row. No FK/unique/check constraint is
bypassed; all original30 assertions remain exact and in order.

`include_feedback_causal` defaults false and requires `include_feedback=true`;
all other optional profiles must be false. The legacy matrix and feedback guard
children explicitly clear the causal flag. Default GREEN parsing and old employee
profiles retain their contracts. Source/fixture/migration pins are checked before
DB setup. Causal execution also checks the actual control checkout HEAD against
CONTROL_SHA and requires clean tracked control files; ordinary profiles retain
their workflow-metadata control binding.

In the existing hosted owned database, the optional phase records the actual
function body/definition, owner, ACL, settings, identity, language and named trigger
state before mutations. It admits exactly eight immutable single-removal variants:
service-role, actor binding, email tuple, active lifecycle, confirmation, ban,
Boolean onboarding marker and registry join correlation. Each private payload
installs its one replacement definition inside the eligibility transaction and
rolls it back. Source hashes bind payloads to the reviewed fixed inventory.

A separate RED parser requires SQL exit0, complete ordered plan31, exactly the
variant's expected failed ordinals, all other assertions successful, no skips,
TODO, bailout, truncation or missing rollback. SQL/setup/permission/process errors
are never expected RED. Each failed ordinal must have its immediately adjacent,
unique pgTAP diagnostic block: matching fixed assertion description, `caught: no
exception`, and wanted SQLSTATE42501 for the service-role assertion or PT403 for
feedback denial. Canonical [pgTAP throws_ok](https://github.com/theory/pgtap/blob/v1.3.0/sql/pgtap.sql.in)
emits only the wanted SQLSTATE in its no-exception branch; the expected message is
bound through the hash-pinned fixture's description/code/message contract. Caught
exceptions, missing/duplicate/malformed or incorrectly bound blocks fail closed.
This format comes from canonical source, not a claimed live causal SQL observation.
SQL definitions containing dollar quotes must be injected literally using a
replacement callback or exact slicing, never a replacement string. Structural
controls require the exact injected definition and reconstruct the original fixture
byte-exact after removing that one span, including one plan and assertion sequence.
Every post-rollback catalog snapshot must exactly match
the actual baseline; there is no compensating restore or retry. First seven
variants require unmodified eligibility31 GREEN and another catalog readback.
The eighth restoration uses the full278 profile, then same-database typegen and
positive owned cleanup. Expected RED observations are never reported as passes:
248 expected-RED assertions,217 intermediate GREEN and278 terminal GREEN (743
across23 executions). Causal receipt qualification additionally requires every
ordered observation, final catalog equality, typegen and lifecycle/cleanup success.

The phase has a monotonic20-minute deadline, zero retries, existing60s packet /
45s statement /3s lock bounds,10s catalog reads and bounded output. Cleanup remains
outside the phase deadline with its existing60s bound and always-cleanup ownership
checks. An unexpected failure stops the phase and retains partial fixed metadata.
Actual timeout/backend drain, catalog restoration and hosted cleanup require the
real admitted run; injected unit ports and synthetic TAP prove only contracts.

The domain regexp is structurally implied by the constrained canonical registry
email plus exact lower(Auth email) matching; it is not a tested mutation or RED.
ACL and missing-registry availability guards are not mutated and retain ordinary
denial coverage. No private recipe, source implementation or positive artifact
activates this optional phase; fresh independent review and parent exact-source /
control hosted admission remain required. Feature activation is separate.

Select `include_journal=true` on the employee schema workflow to apply the full
selected database snapshot and run 324 rollback assertions: the original 172,
48 durable-operation assertions, 61 reserved-preflight assertions, 20 HTTP
runtime-observation assertions and 23 rejection-adjudication assertions. The receipt
uses the `employee-creation-restoration-journal` scope and fails if any packet,
assertion, lifecycle step or cleanup proof is missing. The default remains the
172-assertion foundation profile. This SQL gate does not qualify the fixed worker,
provider, production configuration, generated types or live account operations.

The independent `include_address_migration=true` selection appends three exact
rollback packets, in order: Google destination30, legacy address migration10,
and retained mailbox adoption41. The defaults remain foundation172 and
journal324; the selected totals are foundation253 or journal405. Personal journal
cannot combine with address migration. Its receipt scope adds `-address-migration`
and requires every packet exactly once, in order, with the exact count, no skips,
TODOs, failed assertions or truncation, successful lifecycle and owned cleanup.
The original Google30 and legacy10 packets keep their bytes and ordering.

After all selected address packets pass, the runner generates public, private
and storage definitions from the same isolated database before cleanup. A missing
or malformed generated artifact digest prevents address schema qualification.
The artifact includes `generated-types.ts`; verify its digest against
`generatedTypesSha256` in `qualification.json` before reconciling canonical types.
This does not prove application consumers compile or qualify retained storage
access, provider changes, acknowledgement-loss runtime behavior or account actions.

For SQL-only qualification, dispatch `employee-schema-contract.yaml` with
`include_address_migration=true`, `include_http=false`, and other optional inputs
false. Use a published branch or tag resolving to the reviewed commit as `--ref` and
set `source_sha` to its full immutable SHA. GitHub rejects a raw SHA as the
dispatch ref. Verify the accepted run control SHA equals that source SHA before
moving the ref; the workflow also rejects mismatched address source/control SHAs. An older control that omits adoption41 cannot qualify retained
adoption, even when its source snapshot applies the new migration. Inspect the
run's actual control SHA, exact source SHA, three packet entries and fixture
hashes, generated artifact digest, lifecycle exit and cleanup receipt. A queued,
skipped or failed run establishes no SQL acceptance. HTTP and RESTORE remain
separate transport gates and do not contribute to the SQL count.

The journal, personal journal, feedback and public-consumer profiles retain their
existing same-database type generation. Default foundation selection stays
unchanged. Preserve owned cleanup on generation failure; never substitute source
parser tests, a minimal fixture or manual SQL for the full isolated migration run.

The retained adoption concurrency fixture must connect and drain its independent
writer before the first successful adoption inspection. Those inspections retain
ShareRowExclusive table fences for the rollback transaction; starting the writer
afterward waits behind the fixture itself rather than exercising NOWAIT admission.
The packet asserts no such fence is held before starting the writer, verifies its
actual independent lock, then exercises the original denial without relaxing it.

Conflict fixtures that insert a logical mailbox must link its `domain_id` to the
matching `private.mail_domains` row. The current mailbox trigger rejects an
address-only insert before employee preflight runs. Preserve that trigger and
the intended conflict assertion; a fixture setup failure does not establish a
failure in employee reservation logic.

If the schema runner fails after its private receipt directory exists, the receipt
includes a fixed `failureDiagnostic`: the first failing phase, packet ordinal,
bounded exit status, timeout/signal indicators, and TAP failure flags/counts. It
contains no assertion descriptions, SQL, exception messages, container paths, or
credentials. A diagnostic is evidence about the failed stage, not a passing
packet; verify the same exact source and keep all failed attempts.

The bounded failure diagnostic also records numeric `failedAssertionOrdinals`
only when the TAP numbers are unique, increasing, within the frozen packet's
assertion range, and agree with the failure count. Malformed or oversized evidence
sets `assertionOrdinalsValid` to false and emits an empty array. Match valid numbers
to the exact frozen fixture offline; descriptions and expected/actual values are
never exposed. These numbers locate failures and do not change any passing gate.

### Signup exception contract diagnostics

For failed first-packet assertions 22 and 23 only, the receipt can include the
actual five-character SQLSTATE and a boolean comparison against the fixed expected
message. Caught messages, wanted messages, SQL, identities and TAP descriptions
remain private. Unknown or inconsistent pgTAP diagnostic formats emit invalid
classification with null values; absence of an exception is not inferred. These
diagnostics do not alter the expected 23514 contracts or the strict 172-assertion
success and cleanup gates. The previous timing-only fixture change remained
unqualified after both assertions failed again.

Validated caught records also include a fixed message category for the four
owned creation-denial literals: intent missing, pending required, identity tuple
mismatch, or registry missing. Any other message becomes `other_redacted`.
Unknown or inconsistent diagnostic formats keep the category null. Matching is
exact: whitespace, case, continuation lines and runtime values are never
normalized into an owned category. These enums identify evidence; they do not
change fixture expectations, security checks or schema qualification.

A separate `constraintCategory` classifies six exact generated CHECK-message
relation/constraint pairs from the frozen creation migration: creation-intent
staff email/name and employee staff email/name/lifecycle/recovery. The original
`messageCategory` remains `other_redacted`. Generated messages omit schema, so
schema identity is not inferred. SQLSTATE must be 23514; unknown pairs or altered
text remain `other_redacted`; invalid caught evidence emits null. This diagnostic
does not change SQL, the 25 assertions or the strict 172-assertion success gate.

## Disposable HTTP and Auth qualification

The optional `include_http=true` input requires `include_journal=true`. It keeps
GoTrue, PostgREST and Kong in the same isolated stack, runs all 324 SQL assertions
and type generation, then exercises the actual Web journal, RPC adapter and
provider adapter through loopback HTTP. It creates synthetic identities only in
that disposable project; the entire owned stack is stopped by the existing
cleanup path. No production configuration or activation flag is changed.

The 30 checks cover effective service/anonymous RPC access, successful CREATE,
independent persisted state, stable-UUID replay, payload conflict, a committed
claim with a lost acknowledgement and a successful Auth create with a lost
acknowledgement. Neither unknown outcome may trigger a second provider create.
Credentials enter the child over stdin and never enter its command line or
artifact. Valid failed receipts retain only a fixed phase and completed check count; malformed child output retains only the parent `http-runtime` diagnostic.

`httpTransportQualified` requires a zero child exit, the complete HTTP receipt, all SQL assertions
and successful owned cleanup. It is separate from production proof and does not
qualify the live request authentication boundary, deployed project configuration,
RESTORE, or legacy-address migration. The runtime flag remains off until the
remaining target and request-boundary checks pass. Source tests and a published
workflow are not a successful HTTP qualification run.

## Web request and session qualification

`include_web_session=true` additionally requires both `include_http=true` and
`include_journal=true`. This is an opt-in extension of the same owned disposable
Supabase lifecycle. It builds the selected `apps/web` source on the hosted CI
runner and starts the real Next server on loopback. The fixture resolves the
Next CLI from `apps/web/package.json` so isolated workspace installs do not
require a root Next dependency; Web declares the fixture's Supabase SSR dependency. It does not resume the
retired Docker Web E2E workflow. A missing build prerequisite or failed proxy,
session, SQL or provider check fails this mode; do not replace it with a mocked
authorizer or a service-only receipt.

The Node support-test transform uses the matching
`apps/web/e2e/fixtures/tsconfig.json`, which inherits Web's compiler settings.
Web's main config includes application source rather than these fixtures; without
a matching config, Vite/Oxc can traverse root project references and fail on an
unrelated package's unavailable TypeScript preset before collecting any tests.
The support suite reproduces that failure boundary in a disposable nested tree
and transforms both real fixture files without installing the unrelated preset.
Run `bun x vitest run --config apps/web/e2e/fixtures/vitest.employee-web-session.config.ts`
from the selected source checkout. Passing this finite support suite does not
qualify the 24 hosted Web session cases or the SQL/HTTP/RESTORE profiles.

The fixture sends HTTP requests through the real Web proxy and route handlers.
Its 24 named cases cover absent/malformed credentials, a GoTrue password session
bearer, Supabase SSR-generated cookies, signed infra app cookies, wrong app,
expired and tampered app cookies, canonical actor domain, root membership and
permission revocation, actor ban, GoTrue session sign-out, origin/fetch-site and
action-header guards, self-action, CREATE, RESTORE and stable-operation replay.
App cookies are signed by the production token helper using an ephemeral
fixture secret; this does not qualify the browser login or satellite token
exchange/refresh flow.

The API proxy checks current account assurance before the employee route. A
previously issued satellite cookie whose current provider user is banned is
rejected there with exactly `401 / UNAUTHENTICATED`, before the route's later
`403 / forbidden` actor-policy check. A provider bearer rejected by
`auth.getUser(token)` uses the same exact proxy denial. The actor-ban and
session-sign-out cases require this response, `Cache-Control: no-store`, and no
provider update caused by the denied request; they do not accept interchangeable
401/403 responses or arbitrary error codes. Focused required-MFA runtime tests
exercise both credential paths with injected provider responses. Only the hosted
fixture proves the disposable provider's actual ban and sign-out behavior.

[Supabase getUser](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-getuser)
validates through the Auth server. Sign-out is not proof that an already-issued
access JWT has expired; the fixture retains its bearer and requires the current
provider session check to reject it. A successful source test does not establish
that hosted session-revocation case or all 24 Web cases.

Failed self-action cases retain only the fixed case/stage, numeric HTTP status,
no-store boolean, and an exact allowlisted error category. Unknown codes become
`other`; bodies, identities, headers and tokens are discarded. The strict receipt
accepts this metadata only with the exact completed prefix before self-action,
never as qualification. The self-action expectation remains exactly
`409 / employee_self_action`; the restoration handler regression verifies that
self rejection precedes provider reads, updates and SQL transport. If a hosted
response differs, inspect the fixed metadata before changing that contract.
Passing the injected handler test does not identify an unretained hosted response
or qualify the remaining CREATE/RESTORE cases.

Use `http://localhost:<port>` consistently for the fixture's Web URL and Origin,
while the server continues binding to `127.0.0.1`. Next 16 normalizes loopback IP
request URLs to `localhost`; sending an IP Origin alongside that normalized URL
fails the unchanged origin guard with `403 / forbidden` before self-action or
CREATE. Actual NextRequest handler controls reproduce the mismatch and require
409 for self-action and 201 for CREATE with the matching localhost Origin. A
finite transport control verifies that the localhost URL reaches the IPv4-only
listener. These controls use injected authorization/journal dependencies and do
not replace matching hosted Web24 acceptance. Do not repair this origin mismatch
by granting permissions: the fixture creator retains creator permissions once
its actual MEMBER membership is restored, independently of default grants.

A fixture-only loopback proxy forwards requests to the real owned GoTrue and
PostgREST services. After a successful provider unban it can discard exactly one
acknowledgement; Web must return pending/inspect and reconcile the original
operation without another provider write. A second fault revokes root membership
after the durable attempt acknowledgement and before provider dispatch. The
fixture checks that the target remains banned and no provider update occurred.
These are deliberate network faults around real effects, not mocked auth or RPC
successes. Existing service-level SQL acknowledgement-loss cases remain separate.

`webSessionQualification` records the selected source SHA, completed case names,
assertion count, fixed phase, server-stop evidence and explicit production=false.
Only a complete ordered inventory, zero child exit, matching source, stopped
server/proxy and successful schema lifecycle cleanup can set
`webSessionQualified=true`. Failed or partial cases never establish route proof.
Failed receipts preserve the first fixed runtime phase and error category separately
from server-stop and proxy-close outcomes. Both cleanup steps are attempted even
when the first fails. Build-process diagnostics retain only exit code, a bounded
signal category and deadline status; child output, messages and stacks remain
discarded. Cleanup failure cannot replace an earlier failure or qualify a run.
Compiler stdout/stderr are piped only into two bounded 64-KiB in-memory tails;
they are never printed or written to an artifact. Failed build receipts project
at most eight fixed compiler categories, fixed Node/TypeScript codes, and paths
matched exactly against tracked Web/package source paths. Unknown messages,
module names, identities, config keys and secret values are discarded. Tail
truncation is explicit. Use a matching reviewed source/control revision so the
strict control parser retains these diagnostics. This classification is evidence
for the next investigation, not permission to guess a dependency repair.
Cleanup error categories separately distinguish not-running, type-error, timeout
and unknown; a category never turns failed cleanup into success.

The hosted fixture first runs the existing root Turbo dependency graph with
`bun turbo:local run build --filter=@tuturuuu/web^... --concurrency=1`, then its
unchanged `bun run --cwd apps/web build` real Next compiler. Both phases share
one 18-minute deadline and run sequentially. Prerequisite errors stop the run.
This follows Web's canonical `^build` dependency ordering without allowing an
application cache hit to replace compiler acceptance or filtering the disposable
Auth/runtime configuration out of the direct Web build. Clean installs can resolve
Bun source exports while Node/Next targets still require emitted workspace files;
the non-build export regression demonstrates that boundary without generating
artifacts. Only hosted CI may execute this build pipeline.

Start the resolved Next CLI with `cwd=apps/web` and no additional `apps/web`
argument: `node <resolved-next-cli> start --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port <port>`.
The TypeScript config loader must resolve config imports in the same app context
as the build. A bounded Next 16 config-loader reproduction from the source-root
cwd selected the SEO generator outside the installed source checkout and failed
with a missing-module error; the app cwd selected the source copy and loaded.
The disposable config regression exercises this boundary without an app build,
server or outbound request. Do not repair shared dependencies or infer a hosted
module identity from startup categories alone; matching hosted acceptance remains
required after the launcher correction.

Startup readiness still requires exactly HTTP 401 from the anonymous employees
GET. It makes at most 60 requests (one-second request timeout, 500 ms interval),
never follows redirects, and discards response bodies without buffering them.
The receipt retains only a fixed startup outcome and last observation, numeric
status (0–599), attempt count, child exit/signal and deadline flag. Connection
failure, request timeout, other request error, unexpected status and child exit
remain distinct; an unexpected status does not identify an Auth or routing cause.
Startup stdout/stderr are immediately drained into separate fixed 16-KiB
in-memory prefixes. Only fixed allowlisted categories and a truncation boolean
enter `startupOutput`; raw lines, module names, paths, URLs, headers, bodies and
credentials are discarded. Classification scans each bounded prefix once.
A descendant retaining a writer cannot hold cleanup open: 250 ms after the direct
child exits, remaining capture readers close and truncation is recorded. The
existing TERM/KILL and outer process-group cleanup still govern owned processes.
Truncation or an empty category list cannot clear a possible cause. Loopback controls
exercise these distinctions with disposable children, including the pinned Bun
runtime; they do not establish readiness of the hosted Web application.

The fault proxy starts HTTP server closure before forcing connection closure.
In Bun 1.4.1, forcing connections first stops listening and makes a later
`close()` reject with `ERR_SERVER_NOT_RUNNING`. The finite actual-Bun control
requires successful close, refused connections on the released port, and a
rejected repeated close. It emits only fixed phase/error categories on failure.
Use the workflow's pinned Bun/Node versions when diagnosing runtime differences;
newer local runtime success is not evidence for the pinned runtime.

Historical receipts with only `phase=cleanup` cannot identify the earlier cause.
The support suite exercises simultaneous runtime/cleanup failures, real child exit
and deadline handling, and strict redacted receipt projection. These checks do not
replace hosted Web24 acceptance.

Receipt/process gates run from the uninstalled immutable control checkout; only
`source/` has workspace dependencies installed. Keep process controls on the
canonical dependency-free `.mjs` owner rather than importing the Web TypeScript
support module there. Dependency-bearing adapter tests run in the installed
source checkout. Process controls copy byte-checked canonical modules into a
fresh dependency-free directory, use Bun `--no-install`, and retain all marker,
exit, port/PID and timeout assertions. A control import failure can precede every
build/database/session stage; absent later artifacts do not identify a Web cause.

The control runner owns the fixture process group and launches each requested
build group itself over a private IPC channel. The fixture cannot detach an
unregistered build: missing owner IPC fails closed. Build exit triggers whole-group
TERM/KILL cleanup even when a descendant retains stdout/stderr or ignores TERM.
Fixture exit, hard kill, timeout and cancellation abort and drain every owned build
job before `processGroupStopped` can qualify. Build output is classified at the
owner; only the fixed bounded diagnostic returns over IPC, never raw output.
Actual finite controls retain leader exit 7, enforce an inner deadline, and verify
port/PID disappearance after hard fixture kill and outer timeout. They use the
resolved runtime executable so local command shims cannot drop IPC descriptors.
These synthetic process controls do not replace hosted compiler/start/session proof.
Build/server output, passwords, cookies, tokens, emails and raw provider/SQL
errors are discarded. The stack's always-run cleanup removes fixture identities
with the disposable database; no real account or deployed activation flag is
modified. Source receipt tests prove receipt rejection behavior only. Activation
still requires the parent release owner's review of the actual exact-source CI
artifact and all independent production gates.

### RESTORE transport profile

`include_restore=true` additionally requires both `include_http=true` and
`include_journal=true`. It extends the same disposable project, exact-source
checkout, bounded child and always-run cleanup. The default 324 SQL and 29 CREATE
HTTP checks retain their counts. RESTORE adds 66 checks in seven fixed phases:
RPC permissions (18), success/replay/conflict (11), lost committed reservation,
attempt and completion acknowledgements (8 each), lost successful GoTrue unban
acknowledgement (8), and revoked SQL actor (5). The receipt parser requires every
phase count and a zero child exit before cleanup can qualify RESTORE transport.

The fixture creates managed employees through the real CREATE journal, bans them
through disposable GoTrue, and restores the same user UUID through the retained
RESTORE orchestration and five-function PostgREST adapter. Separate HTTP reads
verify committed operation phase, revision and provider identity. Anonymous and
signed-in outsider credentials cannot execute any of the five RPCs; a service
caller naming an outsider or freshly banned administrator is also denied by SQL.
Lost-acknowledgement injection discards responses only after real commits. Pending
RESTORE and reconciliation retain their operation UUID and never repeat an unban;
completed reconciliation replays the receipt without advancing revision again.

`restoreTransportQualified` is independent of `httpTransportQualified`. It requires
the complete selected SQL/HTTP/RESTORE profile, successful lifecycle and owned
cleanup. This profile calls the retained service orchestration directly; it does
not qualify Web request authentication, satellite sessions, session revocation,
production configuration, hosted races or legacy-address migration. Real GoTrue
transport evidence is distinct from SQL fixture evidence. The RESTORE runtime
flag remains OFF. Dispatch only from a reviewed control revision with the exact
reviewed source commit; a published fixture is not a successful qualification run.

## Personal journal schema qualification

Select `include_personal_journal=true` with `include_journal=false`,
`include_http=false`, `include_web_session=false`, `include_restore=false` and
`include_address_migration=false` on the same workflow. This optional
profile keeps the foundation's 172 assertions and adds the 24
`personal-journal.sql` assertions.
It requires the complete selected migration snapshot, all 196 assertions,
transaction rollback and positive owned-project cleanup, then records the
`personal-journal` scope. Mixed optional profiles fail closed. The default
foundation and employee-operation profiles keep their existing counts. The
workflow regression test exercises all 64 boolean profile combinations against the
guarded runner before hosted database setup.

The same disposable database generates public, private and storage types before
cleanup. Review the exact-source artifact and its digest before adopting generated
types. This gate does not qualify a real journal provider, explicit consent,
authenticated runtime behavior, memory ingestion or production activation.

Before dispatch, keep new, unapplied PR migrations later than the current base
migration tip. The pending personal-journal migration is
`apps/database/supabase/migrations/20261017000000_personal_journal.sql`.
Preserve SQL bytes when correcting only its chronological identity; never rename
an applied migration. A path change changes the selected snapshot and source SHA,
so earlier SQL/type artifacts remain historical and the new source requires fresh
qualification. The isolated runner derives its full snapshot from tracked files,
including the renamed migration, rather than a fixed migration-name manifest.

## Original CREATE response recovery

Infrastructure preserves a validated actor/workspace-scoped original CREATE
operation reference in session storage before dispatch, without a password. If
storage cannot confirm that reference, it does not dispatch CREATE. Pending,
malformed or lost responses trigger bounded TanStack observation reads of
`GET /api/v1/infrastructure/internal-accounts/employees/operations/:operationId`.
This is a CREATE observation contract; employee RESTORE GET/reconcile endpoints
must never substitute for it. A normal confirmed CREATE response incurs no extra
observation round trip.

The GET uses the current Infrastructure session actor and rechecks authorization
before disclosure. Its supplier exposes only readiness/inspection and provider
identity reads. Existing private `employee_creation_runtime_inspect` performs
observation with row locks and no durable writes. Completion requires the exact
operation/target/email/name tuple, an independent confirmed active provider
identity with `employee_onboarding=true`, and a subsequent fresh SQL inspection
of the active account, profiles, personal mailbox/ownership and restricted grants.
A stored phase or earlier receipt alone cannot establish completion. Revoked or
halted operations stop confirmation; absent or incomplete observations remain
unconfirmed. No GET can claim, advance, finalize, activate, reconcile or repeat a
provider operation.

The client admits at most six reads within 30 seconds of the first confirmation read,
with a 500 ms interval and an eight-second client request timeout. Admission
counts and start time survive remounts; reopening cannot reset the budget.
Conflicts remain conflicts, permission denial stops reads, and results from a
retired actor/workspace lifetime are ignored. Unresolved references remain locked
against another CREATE after the budget expires. These bounds describe behavior,
not measured production latency. Readback cannot finish a provider/SQL step that
the original invocation never completed; it can recover confirmation when that
invocation completed despite an uncertain response.

Regression coverage: Web `employee-creation-observation.test.ts` and operation
route tests; internal-api `employee-creation.test.ts`; Infrastructure creation
client/dialog/recovery tests. These synthetic transport and DOM checks do not
qualify real SQL/Auth, deployed authorization, customer creation latency or
production acceptance. The delivery owner must verify exact-commit CI and Web
and Infrastructure builds, then separately collect authorized runtime evidence.

### CREATE password admission

The shared internal-api `EmployeeCreationPasswordSchema` is used by both the
Infrastructure form and Web CREATE boundary. Before readiness or journal claim,
it requires 12–72 characters including an ASCII lowercase letter, uppercase
letter, digit and printable ASCII punctuation. The punctuation set follows
[Supabase password security](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/password-security).
The form explains these requirements in English and Vietnamese and disables
submission until the shared schema accepts the password. It does not normalize,
log or retain the credential in the recovery reference. Boundary regression
controls reject each missing character class before readiness, claim or provider
admission; the internal-api test additionally proves zero HTTP dispatch.

This admission check prevents the observed character-policy mismatch for future
requests. It cannot confirm or repair an existing reservation whose Auth creation
was rejected. The current provider adapter still classifies non-conflict provider
errors, including weak-password rejection, as unknown. Changing that durable
outcome mapping or retiring an earlier rejected reservation requires a separately
reviewed causal recovery contract; observation must continue to report incomplete
state truthfully. Provider-specific rejection (including any additional hosted
policy) is not permission to replay CREATE.

## Administrator adjudication of a rejected initial Auth attempt

An initial CREATE at `unknown` remains non-retryable by default. The service-only
`adjudicate_employee_creation_rejection` RPC is a one-time exception for the
original administrator's terminally rejected first attempt, at version 2. It
requires explicit human attestation of terminal rejection and no request in
flight. Temporal log correlation and account absence are never machine-verified
rejection proof. If the administrator cannot make that determination, retain the
unknown operation and escalate for investigation.

Bind the exact original actor, operation, target UUID, canonical email, name,
expired lease and attempted event. Retain the evidence outside the journal and
supply its SHA-256 reference digest with the fixed adjudication reason. The RPC
freshly authorizes the original administrator, validates both original history
events and the retained intent, and independently checks current Auth identity,
profiles, registry, mailbox, grants and competing reservations. Revocation,
changed identities, later phases, existing repair or conflicting state deny it.
Only service execution is granted; direct audit-table writes are denied.

Success appends a history event and immutable adjudication record and returns the
same operation at reserved/version 3 with an expired replacement fence. It does
not create, activate or prove an account ready. A later explicit normal CREATE
must acquire a fresh lease and use a newly validated password through the existing
journal, provider and persisted completion proof. Never persist credentials,
replay an unknown provider request, delete history or allocate another target.
A lost repair acknowledgement requires inspection; do not blindly retry it.

The journal profile now requires the separate 23-assertion rollback packet
`employee-rejection-adjudication.sql` (324 total). The disposable CLI 2.117.0 pins GoTrue v2.196.0, whose administrator CREATE
path does not enforce password strength. Both HTTP and authenticated Web session terminal rejection controls share the
same invalid-input producer and exact rejection proof. Each control submits
mutually exclusive plaintext and hash inputs, requires exactly HTTP 400 with
`validation_failed`, and independently verifies the selected Auth UUID remains
absent before adjudication. This qualifies terminal rejection recovery, not the
hosted production weak-password policy. Production policy is a separate runtime
observation. See [the pinned Auth guard](https://github.com/supabase/auth/blob/v2.196.0/internal/api/admin.go)
and [the CLI image manifest](https://github.com/supabase/cli/blob/v2.117.0/apps/cli-go/pkg/config/templates/Dockerfile).

Failed rejection HTTP qualification
retains a fixed substep, primary error category, message hash and bounded assertion
value in `httpQualification.rejectionFailure`. Raw SDK errors, response bodies,
addresses and passwords are excluded. The top-level assertion counter does not
identify a failed substep or prove that prior SQL packets passed; inspect the
packet and lifecycle receipts separately. The canonical disposable HTTP
fixture additionally rejects a real weak password through GoTrue, adjudicates
through PostgREST, verifies the committed reservation, denies replay and finishes
normal CREATE with the same UUID. Its strict top-level count is 30. Until that
exact-source fixture and real migration application pass, these are authored
regressions, not runtime qualification or production acceptance.

The Infrastructure stopped-operation panel offers explicit inspection and
adjudication. The authenticated Web recovery route reauthorizes the original
root administrator, binds the full tuple and workspace, and reads back the
committed audit before exposing retry readiness. Session storage retains the
original operation plus repair event/digest before dispatch, never a password.
An uncertain response stays fenced until explicit matching audit readback. Only
then can a user enter a fresh password and explicitly submit normal CREATE with
the original operation UUID and locked email/name. Closing or remounting the
form does not mint a replacement operation.

The optional Web-session profile adds the real authenticated recovery GET/POST
and normal CREATE POST to its ordered case inventory, including revoked-session,
workspace, actor, attestation, origin, tuple and replay denials. The basic HTTP
profile qualifies the lower service/journal boundary; it does not establish
Web request authorization. The selected HTTP fixture typecheck maps the
`@tuturuuu/supabase/next/user` type-only export to its owning source because the
package declaration export otherwise requires unbuilt `dist`. Keep that
source-only gate enabled; do not build locally or bypass type errors.

Select `include_managed_profile=true` with `include_journal=true` on the same reviewed control/source commit.
The runner selects rollback packets `employee-managed-profile.sql` (53), `employee-admin-profile-usernames.sql` (74),
then `employee-unmanaged-profile-usernames.sql` (100), before the committed `employee-managed-profile-concurrency.sql` (10).
Types come from the same disposable database. Username packets exercise changed 1/4/33/65/81/1001-character handles,
null clear, exact ownership, duplicate/CAS/replay denials, unchanged public 5–32 policy and preserved account data.
The legacy packet additionally rejects partial/historical managed evidence, revoked actors and wrong identity/domain;
it preserves disabled/unconfirmed target eligibility, nullable preimages and atomic owned old-handle release.
Only exact protected contexts admit length exceptions; other generic limits and B-tree physical bounds remain.
Optional defaults remain unchanged. `managedProfileQualified` requires all four exact packets, same-run types digest,
base packet success and positive owned cleanup. Missing packets and old receipts cannot qualify.
With `include_http=true`, the managed receipt remains exactly 47 assertions and one lost-ACK write.
Its required `unmanagedProfileQualification` v1 adds 75 assertions, lengths 1/4/33/65/81/1001, six single writes with
lost-ACK independent inspection, exact replay, stale-CAS/duplicate/managed-bypass/ordinary-actor and public-policy denials.
These SQL/PostgREST checks do not establish authenticated Web route composition, browser or production acceptance.
Select the separate default-off `include_profile_route=true` with journal, HTTP and managed profile enabled;
`include_web_session` is not required and its existing creation/restoration matrix is unchanged. The hosted fixture
builds and starts exact Infrastructure source on loopback under the owned process/deadline helpers. Anonymous PATCH
readiness must return 401; GET 405 is not readiness. Real GoTrue sessions traverse the Infrastructure proxy, required-MFA
guard, route authorization, service and managed/null-fallback SQL writers. Each managed and unmanaged target already
owns `hehe`: a name-only PATCH must return 200 with SQL readback and exactly one correctly bound writer RPC;
a competing target must return 409 without SQL state changes. Retained credentials after root revocation or ban,
AAL1 after policy activation, and an invalidated real TOTP proof must be denied without writer calls; real TOTP
verification must pass. Anonymous and malformed Bearer requests cannot borrow a valid cookie. Private SQL snapshots
compare identity, credentials, access, mailbox ownership and creation provenance; receipts publish only fixed diagnostics.
`profileRouteQualification` is independent of the 47/75 transport counts and requires exact source, all 18 cases,
process-group drainage and owned database cleanup. Its `routeAuthorizationProof=true` remains disposable route evidence;
`productionProof=false` always. Direct PATCH imports and mocked authentication cannot qualify this receipt.
